title: Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards Collections Standard: Restriction, Reinstatement and Charge-Off
content:
**Restriction.** Charging privileges on a Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards account are suspended (active to restricted) when the number of consecutive missed minimum payments reaches the card's restriction threshold. The count runs over the statements whose payment due date has passed, walking backward from the most recent one: a statement counts as missed when the payments credited on or after its statement date and on or before its payment due date add up to less than its minimum payment due. A shortfall consisting only of an amount under open billing dispute does not count as missed.

**Reinstatement.** A restricted account is reinstated (restricted to active) on the business day after the payments credited since the restriction cover the entire past-due amount of the latest statement; a payment that is later returned undoes that reinstatement test.

**Charge-off.** A restricted account is charged off when its oldest unpaid minimum payment is the card's charge-off day count past its payment due date, and it is placed with recovery.

**Who acts.** Restriction, reinstatement and charge-off are made by the bank's systems; customer care can explain them but never applies or lifts them.

**While restricted.** The account still receives statements, payments, merchandise credits, dispute handling and AutoPay, but no new purchases and no credit line increases.

## Status path (hypothetical account; restriction threshold 2, charge-off at 180 days)

| Event | Status |
|---|---|
| minimum missed on the April statement | active |
| minimum missed on the May statement too: 2 consecutive misses | restricted |
| payments since the restriction cover the latest statement's whole past-due amount on a Tuesday | active again on Wednesday, the next business day |
| one of those payments is later returned | the reinstatement test is undone |
| oldest unpaid minimum reaches 180 days past its due date while restricted | charged off |

A May shortfall made up only of an amount under open billing dispute would not count as a second missed minimum.
